text:
maria: Hey team — saw a suspicious p99 jump in the canary slice after yesterday's runtime rollout (v2.14.3 -> v2.15.0). Dashboard shows p50 unchanged but p95/p99 up ~2.5x for short-context requests. Deploy window was 2025-11-02 02:15 UTC. Canary was ~10% traffic.

aj: ack. Do you have a link to the time-aligned dashboard and the rollout changelog?

maria: dashboard: https://console.redwood/dashboards/runtime/p99?range=24h — spike starts at ~02:22 UTC. Changelog snippet: kernel-selector change + continuous-batching opt-in for short sequences. Rollout notes included kernel-selection heuristics updated to prefer kernel v3 for certain attention shapes.

sasha: that kernel selector change rings a bell. We saw a similar regression in internal perf runs when we switched heuristics for seq_len <= 64. We adjusted heuristics again but maybe only GA landed in 2.15.0.

jun: can we reproduce locally against the canary binary? If it's kernel selection, trace logs will show which kernel was chosen.

maria: repro steps I used (short context ~16 tokens):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"rwd-small", "input":"Summarize: hi"}'
```
Response latency observed ~420ms p99 during spike window; baseline ~160ms. I captured a small trace with trace_id=trace-0a1b2c.

leo: dumped the trace. Kernel chosen: attention-kernel-v3 for multiple layers, fallback to kv-cache-managed path. Old runtime had attention-kernel-v2 which was faster for short sequences on A100.

nora: support notes: customers started routing tickets about slow single-token completions at ~03:00 UTC. Volume small but consistent. No auth or billing errors reported.

aj: hypothesis: kernel-selector heuristic started preferring v3 for small seqs on certain model dims, but v3 has higher overhead for small token counts on our hardware. Two immediate mitigations: 1) toggle kernel-selector to previous heuristic for canary; 2) rollback canary to 2.14.3 if toggle not possible quickly.

maria: I tried toggling selector via remote config but canary config API returned 409 for that rollout group (config locked by deploy).

deploy-bot: Deployment 2.15.0 to canary completed by @sasha at 2025-11-02T02:15:12Z. Remote config lock: deploy-group-canary (expires in 02:00).

sasha: I can force a patch release 2.15.1 with the selector revert only and push to canary. It'll be a small build, ~12min to verify. Thoughts?

jun: +1 for patch release. Also add a temporary routing rule to divert canary short-context traffic to 2.14.3 if we see customer impact escalate. That buys time.

leo: quick perf diffs I ran on a staging cluster:
```
seq_len=16, model=rwd-small, hw=A100
v2.14.3 p99=158ms
v2.15.0 p99=410ms
v2.15.1 (selector revert) p99=162ms (est)
```
Numbers are averaged but show stark gap.

nora: I'll draft a short customer-facing note for tickets: "We're investigating higher latency for short completions; temporary mitigation underway." Want to avoid alarming enterprise customers but be transparent.

maria: action items: @sasha create patch -> deploy to canary; @jun create routing rule to fallback to prior runtime for short-context requests; @leo gather kernel perf traces across GPU families; @nora prepare ticket message. I'll monitor metrics and escalate if p99 doesn't drop.

aj: add one more: enable verbose kernel-selection debug logging for one canary host to capture decision inputs (seq_len, model_dim, hardware info, latency estimate). Make sure logs are sampled to avoid noise.

sasha: starting patch build now. ETA 12m. Notifying release channel.

ops-bot: Alert: p99 for canary short-context slice > 350ms (threshold 300ms) — triggered at 2025-11-02T02:28:43Z.

jun: routing rule in progress: added hash-based split for requests with context_len <= 32 to route 100% of those requests to runtime-tag:2.14.3 for canary-traffic (temporary). Applying in 30s.

maria: after routing change p99 dropped to ~170ms in the canary slice (observed at 02:31). Looks promising.

leo: perf traces show kernel-selection reverted for those routed requests, using attention-kernel-v2. I'll upload the trace artifacts to the perf bucket: s3://perf-traces/2156001234/

sasha: patch build succeeded. Rolling 2.15.1 to canary now (selector revert). Will monitor for errors.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2.15.1 to canary started by @sasha at 2025-11-02T02:42:10Z.

maria: metrics show sustained p99 reduction after patch rollout; canary p99 back to baseline within 10 mins. No errors reported.

aj: next steps for postmortem: 1) root cause: kernel-selector heuristic change introduced by commit abcdef123 (PR #8342) causing suboptimal kernel choice for seq_len <= 64 on A100 families; 2) mitigation: revert heuristic and add unit perf tests that assert p95/p99 for short contexts when changing selector logic; 3) process: require perf-run gating for kernel-selector changes.

nora: I'll update support tickets with a post-update note: "We've applied a targeted rollback and added safeguards. Expect no further latency regressions; contact us if you still see slow responses."

jun: I'll open a bisect task to find which exact kernel metric threshold triggers the heuristic flip (likely the model_dim threshold). Assigning to @leo.

leo: got it — will bisect across model_dim threshold + check interplay with continuous-batching opt-in.

maria: thanks all. Closing this thread once postmortem doc is linked. For now keep canary at 2.15.1 (selector revert) while we complete perf gating. :thumbsup:

sasha: filing PR for perf gating and adding a short-context regression test harness.

aj: note for ops: consider adding a canary route rule template for quick re-route on latency regressions (we used a hash-based short-context split here). Could be a playbook item.

maria: agreed — will add to runbook.

leo: uploading final traces and a short summary to the incident bucket. Link: https://s3.console.redwood/perf/2156001234/report.html

ops-bot: Incident closed: canary p99 regression mitigated by targeted rollback and routing rule. Severity: low (customer tickets limited). Closed at 2025-11-02T03:10:60Z."
